locked_decisions.summary: Deterministic linter, not an entropy engine. Counting is inside this decision; scoring is outside it.

locked_decisions.status: accepted, DECISION 4 INVALIDATED by the 2026-08-17 proof run — superseding ADR required
locked_decisions.summary: Coverage is measured against declared roots. Workspace-level coverage is not provable by any tool.
locked_decisions.invalidation: Decision 4 makes the ABSENCE of request_status from a paginated list response a hard error. Observed live at Notion-Version 2026-03-11: the field is absent from every normal response (data_sources query has_more true; block children has_more true; block children has_more false). The primary reference documents it as CONDITIONAL, emitted at the 10,000-result cap, with the prescribed test being positive: request_status.type === 'incomplete'. As written, decision 4 hard-errors every healthy scan. Decisions 1, 2, 3, 5 stand. Do NOT edit ADR-0002.
locked_decisions.still_standing: Coverage is measured against declared roots. An unreachable declared root is a hard coverage failure exiting 2. Every unresolvable reference is an explicit observation. The report states start and end times.

locked_decisions.summary: SARIF 2.1.0 as output-contract design source, SonarQube issue-lifecycle as state machine. SARIF is an export target later, not a v0.1 schema commitment.
locked_decisions.superseded_parts: Decision 2 (four-valued outcome enum), decision 3 (`incomplete` fails the run), and the final Consequences paragraph (the SARIF coverage claim). The file was NOT edited — ADR-0005 supersedes those three parts by reference. Decisions 1, 4, 5, 6 stand.
locked_decisions.still_standing: Finding identity is the Notion object ID. Observation/finding split from OSCAL. Baseline entries are never counts. Suppressions require a reason and an expiry, with no escape hatch.

locked_decisions.summary: Determinism defined against a named Normalization function. Specify it before the proof runs.

Outcome is a pair — conformity (conforms|violates, absent when nothing was evaluated) × evidence sufficiency (sufficient|unreached|undecidable). `inapplicable` deleted: operator exclusion moves to the scope declaration, precondition mismatch becomes an applicability filter in the manifest. Report disposition unqualified|qualified|disclaimed; a disclaimed report renders no summary verdict. Coverage manifest is a five-stage funnel: declared, resolved, enumerated, fetched, evaluated.
locked_decisions.governing_rule: A value earns its place only if it changes what the operator does next. This is why evidence sufficiency has three values (different remedies) and why ISA 705's `adverse` was dropped (materiality is not computable by a CLI).
locked_decisions.hard_rule: No ratio is published without the coverage figure bounding it. XCCDF's exclude-from-scoring rule applied alone reproduces the Great Expectations defect — success_percent over evaluated expectations lets a half-unrun suite report 100%.
locked_decisions.pervasiveness_predicate: Gaps are pervasive when a declared root was never reached, or any gap is unbounded. Structural, not a percentage: a ratio threshold would be computed over a denominator the scan has just admitted it cannot establish. Generalises ADR-0002 decision 2.
locked_decisions.deviations_from_checkpoint_plan: Five funnel stages, not four — `enumerated` was added between resolved and fetched because it is the only source of unbounded gaps, and the disclaimed disposition keys on those.
locked_decisions.evidential_standing: Decisions 1-3 rest on adversarially re-verified primary sources (ISA 705 paras 5(a) and 17, XCCDF value list, OSCAL metaschema negative, SARIF schema, PCAOB AS 3105.45, ISO 19011 6.5.1 k, Semgrep enum). Decision 5's funnel shape rests on CONSORT 13a/13b, PRISMA 16b and STROBE 13 — fetched but NOT re-verified, adopted on three-way convergence. Re-verify clause numbers before publishing them.

corrections_pending.claim: Absence of request_status from a paginated list response is a hard error.
corrections_pending.replacement: Test positively: request_status.type === 'incomplete' means the query was cut off. Absence is neither an error nor proof of completeness — it is uninformative, which is the state ADR-0005's `unreached` exists to express.
corrections_pending.urgency: BLOCKS SCAN CODE. This rule sits on the healthy path.

corrections_pending.claim: The coverage claim as currently stated.
corrections_pending.status: OVERSTATED — narrowed by the 2026-08-17 proof run
corrections_pending.replacement: The tool proves coverage of declared roots and resolves links. It CANNOT see permission removal below a declared root: a revoked child vanishes from the parent's child list entirely. Say what is provable and stop there.
corrections_pending.urgency: Before the claim is put in front of a buyer.

corrections_applied.claim: No SARIF object expresses analysis scope or coverage.
corrections_applied.status: REFUTED — corrected in S003, commit db02541
corrections_applied.replacement: SARIF carries per-result and per-artifact not-analysed primitives — result.kind, invocation.executionSuccessful, toolExecutionNotifications, artifact.roles analysisTarget — but defines no run-level coverage aggregate.
corrections_applied.residual: The same refuted sentence still stands in ADR-0002 Consequences and ADR-0003 Consequences. Both are deliberately NOT edited — ADRs are immutable records and ADR-0005 supersedes those paragraphs by reference. Do not 'fix' them.
corrections_applied.decided: Semgrep routes coverage through its native schema, not SARIF. A SARIF export loses the manifest. ADR-0005 §6 accepts that export loss explicitly.

Not provable: anything about permission removal below a declared root, which is silent. This is partial evidence for the wildcard objection in coverage-artifact-prior-art.md section 5.1 — the boundary may be smaller than claimed.

open_decisions.detail: Is the coverage manifest a per-scan artifact or a standing record fed by each scan? MIL-HDBK-61A shows audit outputs flowing back into a standing record of what is under management. If the manifest is produced per scan and discarded, coverage claims can be asserted once but never checked over time.

api_target.requirement: CORRECTED 2026-08-17. request_status is CONDITIONAL, not guaranteed. It is absent from normal responses at Notion-Version 2026-03-11. Test positively for request_status.type === 'incomplete'. Never treat its absence as an error, and never as proof of completeness.
api_target.rate_limit_verified: average of 3 requests per second per connection; workspace ceiling scaled to plan, amount undisclosed
api_target.admin_content_search: Enterprise-only, reaches private pages, exports CSV — but it is a search, not an enumeration. Kill criterion 'Notion ships first-party coverage certification' did not fire.
api_target.notion_version_verified: 2026-03-11 returns HTTP 200 on /v1/users/me — the pin is valid.
api_target.permission_filtering: A page disconnected under a connected parent DISAPPEARS from GET /v1/blocks/{parent}/children. It is not listed-but-unreadable. Verified 2026-08-17 with a full-access control confirming the page still exists at the same ancestor path. An unconnected page returns 404, not 403.

unknowns_assigned_to_proof: ANSWERED 2026-08-17 — NO. A child_page block does NOT stay visible after the child's access is revoked; it vanishes from the parent's child list. The 'detectable hole' does not exist.
Does a property ID survive a property type change? UNTESTED — the fixture has TYPE_CHANGE_PROP=Status ready.

ANSWERED 2026-08-17 — provisionally YES. Two identical paginated queries returned the same 100 IDs in the same order. Fixture-confounded by bulk-created timestamps; re-run against real content before settling.
Does the ~11,200-object search ceiling still hold? UNTESTED — needs a workspace larger than any hand-built fixture.
Is Semgrep's `skipped` output verbose-gated? UNTESTED — a local Semgrep CLI test, nothing to do with Notion.

Do `unreached` and `undecidable` ever diverge in practice? UNTESTED. Note the fixture can no longer produce a permission-caused unreached inside a declared root — that route is closed. Rate limits and abandoned pagination are the remaining routes.
ANSWERED 2026-08-17 — YES, enumeration IS separable from fetching. A 151-block page paged 100 + 51 with has_more and next_cursor. ADR-0005's second Revisit-if does not fire; decision 5 stands.
How often does `disclaimed` fire on a real workspace? UNTESTED — needs REAL_ROOT_ID.
